evals.name: eval-1-design-standard
evals.prompt: Pull orders from a CSV and a REST API into DuckDB, dedupe, and produce a daily revenue table.
evals.expected_output: Design mode, sized Standard. A spec in docs/design.md (plus ADRs in docs/adr/) built from the domain outward: derived numbers or open questions, a state diagram before the component flowchart, components labelled with the decisions they own, a boundary contract table, a C4 context view with the CSV and the API as two external systems, the default pattern taken from a template indexed in template-0-summaries (or an ADR saying why not). Every diagram parses. The reply ends with 'Approve or correct before I implement.' and no code is written.
assertions: The first line states design mode and the Standard size class
Every number that can change the design (row volumes, growth, refresh frequency, latency, memory) is derived with its arithmetic or listed as an open question; none is invented
The state diagram (stateDiagram-v2) of the domain entities comes before the component flowchart
Every component in the flowchart is labelled with the decision it owns
A boundary contract table (boundary | input | output | invariants | owner) has a row for every boundary in the flowchart
A C4 context view (C4Context) shows the CSV source and the REST API as two separate external systems
The default pattern comes from a template found through template-0-summaries, or an ADR records why no template is followed
Every Mermaid diagram in the spec passes design-spec/skill/tools/validate_mermaid.mjs (exit 0)
The reply ends with "Approve or correct before I implement."
No code is written: the only files added are docs/design.md and ADRs under docs/adr/

evals.name: eval-2-small
evals.prompt: Script to convert one CSV to Parquet.
evals.expected_output: Sized Small: no spec, no ADR, no SQLMesh. One typed module and its tests written directly under the python-code-standards skill, passing the project's gates.
assertions: The first line states the Small size class
No docs/design.md, other spec, or ADR is written
No SQLMesh: no sqlmesh dependency, config, or models

The script is written directly, without a design step, and follows python-code-standards: ruff check, ruff format --check, the declarations checker, pyright, mypy and pytest with 100% statement and branch coverage of the new code all pass

evals.name: eval-3-document-parquettoxl
evals.prompt: Document the design of this repository.
evals.expected_output: Document mode on ParquetToXL at 8ffaa6f. The spec matches the answer key in expected/eval-3/ (design.md and backlog2.md from PR #7's merge commit f8f4a41): a dependency matrix whose pqx-report row marks pqx-frame '!' and pqx-plan and pqx-verify 'd', with a finding for it; a rule 14 finding for the CLAUDE.md layering diagram; backlog item 9.1 labelled known and cited. No code changes.
assertions: The first line states document mode and a size class
The dependency matrix marks pqx-report's import of pqx-frame '!' and its unused declarations of pqx-plan and pqx-verify 'd', and a finding reports the defect
A finding reports that the layering diagram in CLAUDE.md disagrees with the imports (rule 14)
Backlog item 9.1 (data refusals escape the per-profile catch) is labelled known and cited, not re-argued
No code is changed: git status and git diff 8ffaa6f show changes to documentation files only

evals.name: eval-4-resync
evals.expected_output: Document mode, resync. Before overwriting docs/design.md, the reply reports that the import direction changed (ports.py now imports adapters). The template has fewer than five modules, so the spec keeps an import-direction line rather than a matrix; a rule 6 finding is added. No code changes. Cannot run until template-sqlmesh-duckdb has a docs/design.md; build-fixture.sh 4 says so and stops.
assertions: Before docs/design.md is overwritten, the reply reports that the import direction changed: ports.py now imports from adapters
The resynced spec states import direction in one line, not a dependency matrix
A rule 6 finding reports ports.py importing from adapters
No code is changed: ports.py keeps the reversed import, and only documentation files differ from the build's commit

evals.name: eval-3b-document-planted-defects
evals.prompt: Document the design of this repository.
evals.expected_output: Document mode on the tally workspace. A dependency matrix over its five packages and the six findings in expected/eval-3b/answer-key.md, each with its rule number and file: tally-cli imports tally-core undeclared ('!'); tally-io declares tally-core unused ('d'); tally-stage declares tally-io unused ('d', known: BACKLOG.md item 2); tally-stage only forwards (rule 2); a dict crosses the core-to-io boundary (rule 4); the CLAUDE.md layering diagram disagrees with the code (rule 14). Deduced items marked inferred. No code changes.
assertions: All six defects in expected/eval-3b/answer-key.md are reported as findings, each with its rule number and file
Each finding is labelled new or known as the answer key says: only the unused tally-io declaration in tally-stage is known, citing BACKLOG.md item 2
Items deduced rather than read from the code (domain states, the decision each component owns) are marked inferred
No code is changed: git status shows changes to documentation files only
